A Letter For You

To our Dad, on his 50th

Fifty years. That's five whole decades of early mornings, big dreams, hard work, terrible jokes, cricket, countless responsibilities, and more love than we could ever fit into a single page — so we made you a whole magazine instead.

Dad, when we look at your life, we don't just see the things you've achieved. We see the journey behind them.

You were the first in the family to dream bigger, to pursue an MBA, to build a career, to buy your own car, and to keep pushing forward even when life wasn't always easy. You built everything step by step, with determination, discipline, and a belief that there was always something more you could do.

And somehow, while building a life for yourself, you were also busy building one for all of us.

You've spent years working hard, taking responsibility, solving problems, and making sure your family had what they needed. Even today, at 50, you're still working, still learning, still helping people, and still finding ways to become better at what you do.

As a sales manager, you've built a career through years of effort. As a nutritionist, you've helped people understand their health and become better versions of themselves. But to us, you've always been something much bigger than any job title.

You're Dad.

The person who somehow has a joke ready for every situation. The person who can turn a simple conversation into a life lesson. The person who worries about everyone, even when you don't say it. The person who keeps going, even when he's tired.

Growing up, we probably didn't always understand how much you were doing for us. We just saw Dad going to work, coming home, giving advice, making jokes, and taking care of things.

Now, as we get older, we understand a little more. We understand that those early mornings meant something. Those long days meant something. Those sacrifices meant something. And every time you put our needs before your own, that meant something too.

You have given us more than things. You've given us an example of what it means to work hard, keep learning, take care of your people, and never stop moving forward.

And Dad, I hope you know how proud I am of you. Not just because of the MBA. Not just because of your career. Not just because of everything you've built. But because after 50 years, you are still you — still dreaming, still working, still laughing, still annoying us with your jokes, and still doing everything you can for the people you love.

So today, for once, don't think about what comes next. Just sit back. Look through these pages. And see yourself the way we see you.

A hardworking man. A dreamer. A provider. A teacher. A nutritionist. A storyteller. A terrible-joke specialist. And most importantly, our Dad.

Happy 50th, Dad. Here's to everything you've built, everything you've taught us, and everything that is still waiting for you ahead.

We love you. ❤️
